chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Zurara, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a servant sins a sin, he is given respite from morning until night; so if he seeks forgiveness from Allah, it will not be recorded against him.'
ai.seo_question: How does seeking forgiveness immediately after sinning affect the recording of sins?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'tawqif' (temporary suspension of recording) in Shia jurisprudence, where a sin is not immediately inscribed in the record of deeds if the servant seeks forgiveness before nightfall. It underscores the divine mercy that allows for immediate expiation, distinguishing between a sin that is merely delayed for potential forgiveness and one that is permanently recorded. This mechanism encourages continuous vigilance and prompt repentance throughout the day.
